blocks.text: An oxidizing agent (atom, ion or molecule) is that substance which oxidizes some other substance, and is itself reduced to a lower oxidation state by gaining one or more electrons, while, a reducing agent (atom, ion or molecule) is that substance which reduces some other substance, and is itself oxidized to a higher oxidation state by losing one or more electrons.
highlight: An oxidizing agent (atom, ion or molecule) is that substance which oxidizes some other substance, and is itself reduced to a lower oxidation state by gaining one or more electrons, while, a reducing agent (atom, ion or molecule) is that substance which reduces some other substance, and is itself oxidized to a higher oxidation state by losing one or more electrons.

blocks.text: If an element M gains one or more electrons and is converted into M⁻ anion, the element M is said to be acting as an oxidizing agent, since it withdraws an electron from the other atom, in this process oxidation number of M has decreased that is:

blocks.latex: \text{For oxidizing agent:}\quad \underset{\substack{[\text{Ox. No.} = 0]\\(\text{Higher Oxidation State})}}{\ce{X}} + \ce{e^-} \ce{->} \underset{\substack{[\text{Ox. No.} = -1]\\(\text{Lower Oxidation State})}}{\ce{X^-}}
blocks.text_alt: For oxidizing agent: X + e⁻ → X⁻ [Ox. No. = 0] (Higher Oxidation State) → [Ox. No. = -1] (Lower Oxidation State)

blocks.text: On other hand, if an element M loses one electron and is converted to M⁺ cation, the element M is said to be acting as a reducing agent, since it is providing electrons, it gets higher oxidation state. Thus,

blocks.latex: \text{For reducing agent:}\quad \underset{\substack{[\text{Ox. No.} = 0]\\(\text{Lower Ox. No.})}}{\ce{M}} \ce{->} \underset{\substack{[\text{Ox. No.} = +1]\\(\text{Higher Ox. No.})}}{\ce{M^+}} + \ce{e^-}
blocks.text_alt: For reducing agent: M → M⁺ + e⁻ [Ox. No. = 0] (Lower Ox. No.) → [Ox. No. = +1] (Higher Ox. No.)

blocks.prompt:
a) Identify the oxidized species and reduced species in the following equation. Also identify the oxidizing and reducing agents on the reactant side.
i. Fe₂O₃(s) + CO(g) → Fe(s) + CO₂(g)
ii. CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l)
blocks.explanation:
i. Fe goes from +3 to 0 (reduced) and C from +2 to +4 (oxidized): Fe₂O₃ is the reduced species and the oxidizing agent; CO is the oxidized species and the reducing agent.
ii. C goes from −4 to +4 (oxidized) and O from 0 to −2 (reduced): CH₄ is the oxidized species and the reducing agent; O₂ is the reduced species and the oxidizing agent.

blocks.prompt:
b) Identify the species in the following reaction which undergoes both oxidation and reduction.
i. 3HNO₂(aq) ⇌ HNO₃(aq) + 2NO(g) + H₂O(l)
ii. P₄(s) + 3OH⁻(aq) + 3H₂O(l) → PH₃(g) + 3H₂PO₂⁻(aq)
blocks.explanation:
i. N is +3 in HNO₂; it becomes +5 in HNO₃ (oxidation) and +2 in NO (reduction), so HNO₂ is both oxidized and reduced.
ii. P is 0 in P₄; it becomes −3 in PH₃ (reduction) and +1 in H₂PO₂⁻ (oxidation), so P₄ is both oxidized and reduced.
